## Product description (Amazon "Book description", about 190 words)
In 2024, nearly 144,000 American adults were listed for a kidney transplant. In the same year, almost three of every ten kidneys that surgeons and coordinators managed to recover were never transplanted. Nobody in the system is a cartoon villain. So why does the machine waste so much, so reliably, year after year?

The Cooler and the Clock is an audit. Using the Lean Six Sigma method that transformed factories and hospitals, Jeff Parke defines the customer nobody surveyed, maps a process no single office owns, measures the defects, and analyzes their causes: decisions that vary from one clinician to the next, incentives that reward the wrong things, a trust that can vanish in a week, and a living-donor pathway that quietly depends on household finances.

Every claim is sourced and graded. Fact is separated from finding, allegation, and rumor. The newest developments of 2026 are examined alongside the evidence on cold ischemia, perfusion technology, oxygen carriers, and the first pig-kidney trial. The book closes with a twelve-point reform platform, a control plan, and ten questions patients can ask tomorrow. Written for patients, care partners, clinicians, policymakers, and anyone who believes a system that can be measured can be improved.

## KDP steps that are the author's to do
1. Create the title in KDP. When asked whether the content was AI-generated or AI-assisted, answer truthfully; KDP requires this disclosure for text, images, and cover art, and it applies to this manuscript.
2. Choose the free KDP ISBN or supply your own. Confirm the copyright holder and publisher line on the copyright page (currently "Copyright © 2026 Jeff Parke" and "Published by the Cold Ischemia Foundation").
3. Upload the EPUB (or the DOCX) and the cover.jpg; run the KDP Previewer on phone, tablet, and e-reader views.
4. Optional: Kindle Create can import the DOCX and produce a KPF file if you prefer a Kindle-native build.

## Verification still owed (the manuscript is honest about each)
The research tools available while writing returned search-result summaries, not the full text of journals or agency pages. Every claim is therefore tied to a graded entry (Appendix A), and sources marked † need author lists, titles, or volume details completed from the originals. Before the first edition goes live:
1. Complete every † reference from the original document.
2. Confirm the ten-year machine-perfusion follow-up (manufacturer press release only) and the HEMO2life figures (preliminary; reconcile registry numbers).
3. Re-check anything dated after 9 October 2026: organ-procurement tier outcomes and the final rule, first-year results of the transplant access payment model, and the enacted Medicaid provisions.
4. Confirm the 2025 living-donor count against the registry (single news source).
5. Consider a short legal review of Chapters 10 and 9 (the Kentucky investigation, the Miami decertification, and the governance discussion). The text uses the cited wording of federal documents and labels allegations as allegations, but legal review is the responsible final step for any book that names organizations.
